geological_stratigraphy.why: a vertical rectangular column divided into horizontal segments of different colours, with a depth scale on the left (0m to 32m) and labels on the right indicating soil types.
geological_stratigraphy.subject: A vertical soil profile diagram highlighting the specific 'soft blue clay' layer at depth compared to the stable surface soil.
geological_stratigraphy.title: Subterranean Soil Layers

rotational_stability_analysis.why: A tilted rectangle divided into three horizontal bands, a horizontal axis with numerical markings (-8m to +8m), a dashed vertical line extending from the rectangle to a red dot below the axis.
rotational_stability_analysis.subject: An animation showing the building tilting and the center-of-gravity vector moving outside the foundation's base, demonstrating the risk of toppling.
rotational_stability_analysis.title: Shifting Center of Gravity

subsurface_geology_interaction.why: Three horizontal soil layers separated by dashed lines with a tilted yellow rectangle extending into the bedrock layer.
subsurface_geology_interaction.subject: A diagram showing the tilted foundation hitting a denser, resistant soil layer, acting as a physical pivot or barrier.
subsurface_geology_interaction.title: The Soil Stopper Effect

molecular_clay_structure.why: Four horizontal light-blue bars stacked vertically, with small dark circles labeled 'H2O' positioned between them, and small red circles with minus signs at the ends of each bar.
molecular_clay_structure.subject: An animated microscopic view showing flat plates with trapped water molecules and electrical charge indicators.
molecular_clay_structure.title: Clay Particle Microstructure

pore_pressure_process.why: a red rectangle above four horizontal grey bars, with several small blue dots scattered between the bars and to the right, and a yellow line indicating an exit path to the right.
pore_pressure_process.subject: An animation showing water being squeezed out from between clay plates as weight is applied, representing the pressure increase.
pore_pressure_process.title: Excess Pore Water Pressure

shear_failure_diagram.why: A rectangular cross-section divided into three horizontal layers labeled Topsoil, Clay Layer, and Bedrock, with a tilted red rectangle labeled 'BUILDING' resting on the surface, and a dashed yellow curved line extending from the surface down through the layers to a red arrow labeled 'Slip Plane'.
shear_failure_diagram.subject: A cross-section diagram showing the building sliding along a curved, subterranean 'slip plane' path.
shear_failure_diagram.title: Circular Shear Failure

underpinning_process.why: A horizontal structure sitting above a soil layer and a bedrock layer, with four vertical yellow columns extending from the bedrock through the soil to the structure, topped by red triangles and a dimension line labeled 54 ft.
underpinning_process.subject: A diagram showing the proposed concrete piers extending down to bedrock, illustrating how they would act as jacks to lift the tilted structure.
underpinning_process.title: Proposed Pier Restoration

aquifer_cross_section.why: A stack of four horizontal rectangular layers labeled Topsoil, Clay Cap, Gravel Aquifer, and Bedrock, with a vertical dashed yellow line and a red dot indicating a point of penetration through the clay into the aquifer.
aquifer_cross_section.subject: A cross-section showing the pressurized water layer trapped beneath the clay, illustrating why digging into it is dangerous.
aquifer_cross_section.title: Hidden Artesian Aquifer

hydrostatic_failure_simulation.why: A vertical cross-section of three horizontal layers (topsoil, clay barrier, aquifer) with a central shaft containing upward-pointing arrows and a red dot at the base of the shaft.
hydrostatic_failure_simulation.subject: An animation showing a drill hitting the aquifer and water rapidly forcing its way up into the excavation shaft.
hydrostatic_failure_simulation.title: Artesian Water Breach

thermal_bridge_flow.why: A vertical white bar between two dark rectangles, with red arrows pointing right and blue arrows pointing left at the top and bottom edges.
thermal_bridge_flow.subject: Red arrows representing heat flow from the interior through a glass pane to the outside, while blue 'cold' arrows creep inward along the window's edge.
thermal_bridge_flow.title: The Thermal Bridge Effect

window_spacer_conduction.why: Two vertical rectangles connected by a horizontal bar, a vertical axis with temperature markings from -10°C to 21°C, downward arrows, and a color gradient from light gray to blue in the vertical shapes.
window_spacer_conduction.subject: A cutaway of a double-pane window highlights the internal aluminum spacer bar glowing bright blue as cold temperatures conduct rapidly into the glass edges.
window_spacer_conduction.title: Spacer Bar Cold-Sink

material_moisture_seepage.why: Two groups of irregular horizontal shapes with a blue-to-grey color gradient, a horizontal axis with millimeter markings, small blue dots, and a legend identifying moisture and substrate.
material_moisture_seepage.subject: A microscopic cross-section of wood and drywall shows blue liquid molecules migrating into the jagged internal pores of the material fibers.
material_moisture_seepage.title: Sub-Surface Moisture Absorption

surface_tension_comparison.why: a split screen with a semi-circular shape on a horizontal bar on the left, a thin flat rectangle on a horizontal bar on the right, directional arrows, and numerical angle values (105° and 12°).
surface_tension_comparison.subject: A split-screen view compares a high-tension water bead on untreated glass against a flattened, horizontal sheet of water on a soap-treated surface.
surface_tension_comparison.title: Surface Tension Modification

thermal_viscosity_trap.why: a grey vertical bar, a brown rectangle, small blue circles at the interface, rows of larger white circles, and a temperature scale with a pointer at 47.3°F
thermal_viscosity_trap.subject: As the solution hits a cold glass surface, the liquid molecules stop moving and cluster together, trapping blue vapor bubbles underneath the layer.
thermal_viscosity_trap.title: Temperature-Induced Solution Failure
